candidates.label: Mysia (label point)
candidates.support: Mysia's identity as the region in the northwestern corner of Asia Minor is undisputed. The label point is Pleiades' dedicated entry for the region, cross-checked against Wikidata's own point about 72 km to the northeast.

summary.text: Mysia was a region of northwestern Asia Minor whose boundaries, the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia notes, were never clearly fixed; it names Assos, Troas and Adramyttium, all mentioned in the New Testament, among its cities, though only some authors counted the Troad as part of Mysia. Acts records that 'when they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn't allow them,' so 'passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.'

history.text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia describes Mysia as a major part of the province of Asia, and its article on Asia lists Mysia among the older countries the province included and dates the province's formation to 129 BC. At this project's about AD 50 date, Mysia therefore lay within the province of Asia.

scripture.textWEB: When they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn’t allow them.
Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
